newsitem.title: USA: Bungee jump at Super Bowl canceled after fatality.
newsitem.headline: Bungee jump at Super Bowl canceled after fatality.

text.p: A bungee-jumping stunt planned for the finale of Sunday's Super Bowl half-time show was cancelled on Friday, 13 hours after an entertainer rehearsing the act died of massive head injuries.
National Football League Commissioner Paul Tagliabue told a news conference, "That part of the finale will be omitted from the show for obvious reasons."

Earlier on Friday he said authorities did not know why Laura Patterson, 43, of Sarasota, Florida, hit the floor with her head. She was pronounced dead of massive head injuries at 10:25 p.m. CST (0425 GMT) at Charity Hospital, he said.

Although details have not been finalised, he said, "We will take note of Mrs. Patterson's death and commemorate her life." He said an investigation was under way to determine if the accident was caused by human error or equipment failure.
A witness said the cord did not break and Patterson was still attached to it but limp when the cord snapped her body back up into the air after the jump, police said.

Tagliabue said she was part of a 16-member professional bungee-jumping team that performed like a circus act. Nine members were to jump from the terrace level of the indoor stadium during the last 30 seconds of the half-time show.
The victim's husband and sister, who are part of the team, were present when the accident occurred.

The troop had been rehearsing for three days and Patterson hit the arena floor several times near the 50-yard line on the team's third jump of the night, Tagliabue said. Most of the other cast members for the half-time show were facing in another direction when the accident happened and initially were unaware of it, he added.
Volunteer stagehand Eddie Chelette said many of the children in the cast were visibly upset later. "The school kids who were dancing were crying. Everyone else was walking around in a daze."
